row.evidence: Expo's pricing page lists Single sign-on (SSO) on Production ($199/month) and Enterprise only, and the SSO docs describe OIDC sign-in where users pick an Expo username on first login; no SCIM endpoint is documented.
row.notes: New row; researched as Expo Application Services (EAS) accounts. Plans are flat per account per month plus usage (Free $0, Starter $19, Production $199, Enterprise custom; members unlimited on every plan), so per-user prices are null; only monthly prices are shown. OIDC SSO (Okta, OneLogin, Entra ID, Google Workspace via customer-created apps) is on Production and Enterprise; SSO users are created on first sign-in (JIT) with the View Only role, and removing a user in the IdP only cuts access after the IdP token refresh window (an admin can 'Delete SSO user' in Members). No SCIM or member-management API is documented; robot users and access tokens are for EAS CLI/CI actions. Audit logs are Enterprise-only (dashboard, export, eas account:audit CLI). The Trust Center says SSO is for 'Enterprise subscribers', which conflicts with pricing and docs (Production). 'None' is by absence (rule 5).

plans.name: Starter
plans.notes: Free plan ($0) also allows unlimited members; Starter is the cheapest paid tier. scim false is by absence.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Audit logs readable via dashboard export or the eas account:audit CLI command; no REST audit API documented.

scim.notes: No SCIM page in docs.expo.dev sitemap (1,780 URLs), llms.txt or llms-full.txt, expo.dev sitemap, pricing page, security or trust pages. Provisioning is OIDC JIT only. 'false' is by absence (rule 5).

audit_log_api.notes: Audit logs are Enterprise-only and can be read programmatically with the eas account:audit CLI; no REST endpoint is documented.

limitations.text: Robot users and access tokens act on account resources through EAS CLI; no member-management endpoints are documented.

user_api.notes: No public member/user-management API is documented. Personal access tokens and robot users authenticate the EAS CLI for builds, submits and updates.

okta.notes: Expo's Okta guide has the admin create their own OIDC app ('Create App Integration'); okta.com/integrations/expo/ returned 404.

entra.notes: Expo's Entra guide uses an App Registration; learn.microsoft.com expo-tutorial returned 404.

google.notes: Google Workspace is a supported OIDC IdP (customer-configured); Marketplace listing not checked.

onelogin.notes: OneLogin is a supported OIDC IdP per Expo; OneLogin catalogue not checked (bot-blocked).
